question.text: The specific heats, <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub></math> of a gas of diatomic molecules, <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>,</mo></math> are given (in units of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> ) by <math><mn>29</mn></math> and <math><mn>22</mn><mo>,</mo></math> respectively. Another gas of diatomic molecules, <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>,</mo></math> has the corresponding values <math><mn>30</mn></math> and <math><mn>21</mn><mo>.</mo></math> If they are treated as ideal gases, then:

options.text: <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> has one vibrational mode and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> has two
<math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> has a vibrational mode but <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> has none.
Both <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> have a vibrational mode each.
<math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is rigid but <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> has a vibrational mode.

solution.text:
For A :
R=Cp-Cv=29-22=7
Cv=fR2
⇒22=f×72
⇒f=447=6.3
⇒f≈6

(5 rotational + translational, 1 vibrational)


For B :
R=Cp-CV=30-21=9
Cv=fR2=21
⇒f=21×29=429=4.66≃5
∴ f≃5

 (5 rotational + transitional, 0 vibrational)
